notesForTheArchitect: My miss, stated so the retro has it from the phase that made it: round four's check of pr-body.md was a diff against main, which cannot show content main added that this branch ought to delete. A forward merge keeps both sides, so a deletion this branch made to a paragraph main later rewrote comes back in silence, with no conflict and no marker. The control is to diff the branch's pre-merge head against its own fork point and check every removed line against the tree as it stands - which found nothing else this round, and is the check I would add to skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md beside the fingerprint, since the fingerprint answers 'did the branch's diff change' and this answers 'did the branch's deletions survive'. They are not the same question: this regression changed the fingerprint legitimately, because two fix commits landed with the merge.

One false positive in the new guard, fails closed, not a failure and not worth a round: its comment claims a sentence naming the line while saying it is gone cannot reach the instruction slots, and five of the six shapes I probed pass as claimed ('carries no `CI:` line', 'never writes the `CI` line' including across a line wrap, 'wherever the CI line is quoted', 'there is no `CI:` line to fill', 'no longer cited from the `CI` line'). The sixth does not: 'nothing is cited from the `CI` line any more' fires, because the negator is a negative subject rather than one of never|no longer|not in the lookbehind. The guard refuses it, so nothing escapes; what is slightly wrong is the comment's claim about its own blind spot, and the cost is a future author rephrasing one sentence. Worth a fast-follow line rather than a round.
